issues: Covers and spend per head both rose, with omakase bookings lifting spend, but sales remain far below target.
Labour rose because of intensive training.
Stock recording is inaccurate, particularly for soft drinks, and staff are not consistently recording drinks and catalogue items in the system.
A delivery of 200 kilograms of sugar was accepted instead of 20 kilograms and was not returned.
Role boundaries between the two senior kitchen staff are unclear, creating grey areas in stock control and ordering; a meeting with Sophie is to be arranged to define responsibilities.
A printer moved to the counter near the till has no power because of a shortage of sockets; an extension cable is due on Thursday.
The bar varnishing and painting schedule is still unconfirmed by the external vendors.
Ross confirmed the house plum wine method: layer rock sugar with plums, sugar on top, buy supplies from the Chinatown shop and shake the jars daily.
A team member is off and is expected back on Sunday.
Staff need to be more proactive in asking customers for reviews.
Maintenance: the sushi bar is held up by a fridge, the walls need painting and the floor needs coating.
Hygiene compliance improved on the prior week and all waste was tracked.
Deep cleaning continues: floor tiles, bathrooms and the restaurant front are done and the wooden flooring is in progress.
Pest control advised re-boarding the sushi hand wash section, with a revisit in seven days.
Front of house labour is being held with only two front of house staff all day on Mondays and Tuesdays, long breaks for everyone and reduced head chef hours.
Service standards and teamwork are the main areas for improvement.
Omakase nights run on Thursday and Friday, and lunch promo materials and new drinks menus will go out on bill trays as a talking point.
Region-wide (South England): Staff must explicitly confirm pork ingredients and dietary requirements with customers when taking orders, rather than making assumptions from appearance.
Region-wide (South England): Right to work checks must be fully cleared before any new starter is scheduled for a shift.
